# CodexMeter 1.4.8
A bug-fix release, plus the repository move to its canonical location.
## What changed
- **Turning Claude off now always wins over an in-progress account add.** If you disabled Claude Code while an account add was still checking, the add could finish a moment later and reinstall CodexMeter's status-line helper into `~/.claude/settings.json` — right after the disable had removed it. The disable now blocks any in-flight add or refresh from completing. - **The repository and update feed point at their canonical `dlfkdLR/CodexMeter` location** after the GitHub account was renamed from `HechoLP`. New builds check `raw.githubusercontent.com/dlfkdLR/...`, and the in-app GitHub links, README, and Homebrew tap references use the new owner. Existing installs keep working through GitHub's redirects — nothing to do.
No change to signing keys, saved-account storage, automatic-update behavior, or the check schedule.
## Verification
- 292 automated tests, 0 failures (7 environment-integration tests skipped); the Claude disable/add race is now covered by a timing-independent test. - `swift build` with zero warnings and zero errors. - Universal 2 build for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later; the bundled Claude limits helper is signed and verified as part of the release. - The app remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-notarized. SHA-256 protects the first download; Sparkle authenticates later update feeds and archives with Ed25519 signatures.
## Install or update with Homebrew
```bash brew update brew upgrade --cask --greedy dlfkdLR/tap/codexmeter ```
For a new installation:
```bash brew install --cask dlfkdLR/tap/codexmeter ```
If macOS blocks this certificate-free app after installation, confirm that it came from `dlfkdLR/tap/codexmeter`, then remove quarantine from this app only:
```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CodexMeter.app open /Applications/CodexMeter.app ```
## First direct-download launch
Download `CodexMeter-1.4.8.dmg` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` from this release into the same folder. Verify the checksum before opening the disk image:
```bash cd ~/Downloads grep ' CodexMeter-1.4.8.dmg$' SHA256SUMS.txt | shasum -a 256 -c - open CodexMeter-1.4.8.dmg ```
Only after the checksum reports `OK`, copy `CodexMeter.app` to Applications and use the app-scoped quarantine command above.
## Recovery
This release does not migrate any database. Published version tags are immutable; corrections ship as a new patch release.
